pets.title: Finding “the dog is easier” than the people at home, and uneasy about it
pets.description: Drawn home by a welcome nobody else gives her, from a dog who will never grow away from her, glad of the dog as a way round rows and hard talk, and unsure what that says about her and her partner

pets.title: Drawn home by a welcome nobody else gives her
pets.description: Once she found reasons to stay out, and now she comes home for the door, which her partner has noticed

pets.title: A morning grievance the dog takes away unsaid
pets.description: Always the one who gets up, and the mood gone by the bottom of the stairs

pets.title: Half nine: closer through the dog, or talking about her “instead of talking”
pets.description: The dog keeps them in one room and laughing, and is a way out of the list, and she cannot say which

pets.title: Home “never empty” with the dog, and its loss already rehearsed
pets.description: The dog at the centre of home, felt most when she is out of it, and a false alarm that showed her grief ready and waiting

pets.title: The dog at the centre of home, felt most in her absence
pets.description: Never empty with her, and two hours without her a wrong quiet in a house that waits

pets.title: Grief for the dog rehearsed on a false alarm, then pushed away
pets.description: Shaking on the drive to the vet, crying in the car park, and the thought of the end not let finish

pets.title: “Caught” going soft for the dog she said no to
pets.description: Won over against her picture of herself, through a first year's regret she never said, to a walk of her own and a closeness that costs her

pets.title: Won over against her picture of herself
pets.description: Not a soppy person, she thought, and now goodnight said out loud

pets.title: A first year's regret, too terrible to say and never quite gone
pets.description: Her time no longer hers, a mistake thought and kept silent, and back on wet nights

pets.title: A walk once resented, now “the bit of the day that is mine”
pets.description: Forty minutes nobody can claim, beside a dog's joy in a wet hedge

pets.title: A wordless closeness, proved by what it costs her
pets.description: Closest on the worst night, an understanding with no word said, and the worry of letting her run

Initial:3:0.text: A house never empty with the dog, even when quiet
quotes: "I suppose she is just there. That is the first thing. Bramble is just there, all the time. … The house is never empty now. Even when it is quiet it is not empty."
notes: Twice: just there. The stair is a boundary kept without being asked for. Quiet and empty come apart here, so presence is felt rather than seen.

Initial:5:0.text: Caught out going soft over the dog
quotes: "It is like being caught. I am not a soppy person, or I did not think I was. … And I have started groaning back at her. That is the state of me now."
notes: Caught, as if found out. Four years of no dog, then a whole conversation in a dressing gown. She laughs at the state of herself and keeps groaning back.

Initial:7:0.text: Won over by the dog before she would admit it
quotes: "once you have seen a photograph like that you have already lost the argument, you just have not admitted it yet. … I still say I was talked into her, and my partner still says I was the one who filled the form in, and we are both right."
notes: The photograph wins before the argument is over. Two stories of who decided, and she keeps both. The lean in the yard is the lean at the door now.

Initial:11:0.text: Always the one up for the dog, and feeling taken for granted
quotes: "Annoying. No, it is more than annoying. … It is what the twelve minutes says. That I will always go. That they know I will always go, and so they can lie there and let me."
notes: She corrects her own word upwards. Twelve minutes stand for for ever. The wag takes the annoyance away, and losing it is its own annoyance.

Initial:13:0.text: Anger taken off her by the dog, so it never gets said
quotes: "But you cannot carry a mood down those stairs. She takes it off you at the bottom. … So it never gets said. Five years of it never getting said."
notes: A mood cannot be carried down those stairs. What goes unsaid between the two of them is counted in years.

Initial:17:0.text: From resenting the morning walk to loving it as her own time
quotes: "I love it. I did not expect to hear myself say that. The first year I resented it, I really did, I thought, this is forty minutes I have not got. And now it is the bit of the day that is mine."
"Nobody can ask me for anything, because I am out with the dog, and that is a completely respectable reason to be unavailable. Nobody argues with it."
notes: Resentment turned to love over the years, and it surprises her to say so. Out with the dog nobody can ask her for anything. Her head goes quiet by watching, not by thinking.

Initial:17:1.text: Glad to be out of reach with the dog
quotes: "I love it. I did not expect to hear myself say that. The first year I resented it, I really did, I thought, this is forty minutes I have not got. And now it is the bit of the day that is mine."
"Nobody can ask me for anything, because I am out with the dog, and that is a completely respectable reason to be unavailable. Nobody argues with it."
notes: Resentment turned to love over the years, and it surprises her to say so. Out with the dog nobody can ask her for anything. Her head goes quiet by watching, not by thinking.

Initial:19:0.text: The dog's joy quieting her head and her moods
quotes: "But there is something about how much she is enjoying it. … And you cannot stand next to that much enthusiasm for a hedge and stay in a bad mood, it is not possible."
"It is a bit like being with a small child, except she is not going to grow out of it and start being embarrassed by me."
notes: Ten past seven, in February, every morning. The joy is the dog's and it reaches her. The child she compares her to never grows up and away.

Initial:19:1.text: The dog like a child who will never grow away from her
quotes: "But there is something about how much she is enjoying it. … And you cannot stand next to that much enthusiasm for a hedge and stay in a bad mood, it is not possible."
"It is a bit like being with a small child, except she is not going to grow out of it and start being embarrassed by me."
notes: Ten past seven, in February, every morning. The joy is the dog's and it reaches her. The child she compares her to never grows up and away.

Initial:21:0.text: The dog's joy worth the worry
quotes: "I have watched her go across that field after a hare and it is one of the best things I have ever seen, and I am furious the entire time it is happening. … because the look on her at full stretch is worth more to me than the twenty minutes of worry."
notes: One of the best things she has seen, and furious the whole time: two at once again. She weighs it up every morning and always lets go.

Initial:23:0.text: Regretting the dog in a hard first year, her time no longer hers
quotes: "The first year was hard. I had not reckoned on how much of my time stopped being mine. … And there was a stretch, maybe six months in, where I thought, I have made a mistake here. I did not say that out loud to anybody."
notes: Not the money but the freedom. A weekend away becomes a logistics operation. The mistake is thought, and kept silent.

Initial:25:0.text: Unable to say she regrets a dog with a hard past
quotes: "Because it is a terrible thing to say, isn't it. She is a rescue. She had a rough time of it before us, you can still see it in her, she flinches if you move your arm too fast above her head, even now."

"So I did not say it, and then it went away, mostly, the way things do. But I would be lying if I told you it never comes back. It comes back on a Sunday night in February when it is chucking it down"
notes: Saying it would be terrible because of what the dog has been through. It went away, mostly. On a wet Sunday at ten it comes back.

Initial:25:1.text: The regret gone, mostly, but back on wet winter nights
quotes: "Because it is a terrible thing to say, isn't it. She is a rescue. She had a rough time of it before us, you can still see it in her, she flinches if you move your arm too fast above her head, even now."

"So I did not say it, and then it went away, mostly, the way things do. But I would be lying if I told you it never comes back. It comes back on a Sunday night in February when it is chucking it down"
notes: Saying it would be terrible because of what the dog has been through. It went away, mostly. On a wet Sunday at ten it comes back.

Initial:27:0.text: Moved by the dog waiting on her decision
quotes: "And she was sat behind me, completely still, not pushing at me, not doing the whine, just waiting to see what I decided. That is the bit that got me, actually. She was not begging. She was just waiting."
notes: Stillness on both sides of the porch. That the dog waited without pushing is what got her. The turn at the postbox is made by neither of them.

Initial:29:0.text: Closest to the dog on the night it cost her
quotes: "I think because it cost me something. That sounds a bit grand. But the easy days do not prove anything, do they."
notes: She hears herself sound grand and says it anyway. Cost as proof. Failing together turns into a bargain struck by the postbox.

Initial:31:0.text: Unspoken rules with the dog, strange to have
quotes: "There are rules in that house and neither of us wrote them down. That is a strange thing to have with another creature, when you stop and think about it. We have never once had a conversation and we both know exactly where we stand."
notes: The joke first, then the list of the rules. An understanding with no conversation, which strikes her as strange once she stops to think.

Initial:33:0.text: The dog's welcome home the best bit of her day
quotes: "Oh, it is the best bit of the day, without question. … She puts her whole weight against your legs and stands there with her head down."
notes: Coming home given in sound first, then in weight. The same lean as the yard five years ago. The rabbit muffles the whine.

quotes: "It is being wanted. Plainly. Nobody else in my life is that pleased to see me, and I say that with no bitterness at all, it is just a fact."
notes: Plainly, and with no bitterness, she insists. The hello from the other room is set beside it: fine, what adults do.

Initial:37:0.text: From finding reasons to stay out to coming home for the dog
quotes: "There was a stretch where I would find reasons to stay out, nothing dramatic, just one more thing to sort out before I left. And now there is a clock on me. … But I want the door bit. So I come home."
notes: A stretch of staying out, said lightly, nothing dramatic. Now she wants the door bit. Her partner has noticed.

Initial:39:0.text: Unsettled by her partner's remark that she comes home for the dog
quotes: "And they were pleased, I think, they meant it nicely. But there was something else in it as well, which was, you will come home for the dog. And I did not know what to do with that. Because it is true."
notes: Said nicely and heard twice over. She does not know what to do with it, and will not deny it.

Initial:41:0.text: Finding the dog easier than people, and not liking what that says
quotes: "The dog is easier. That is the thing I keep landing on and then moving off, because it is not a nice thing to think about yourself. She does not need me to have got anything right."
notes: The thought she keeps landing on and moving off. The dog needs nothing to have been got right. With a person the past is stood in the hall as well.

Initial:43:0.text: Unsure whether the dog is good for the couple or a way of not talking
quotes: "Either it means she has been very good for us … Or it means we have found something to talk about instead of talking. And I genuinely do not know which one it is."
notes: Two readings held open, good for us or a way round each other. Some weeks the one, some weeks the other.

Initial:47:0.text: Shaken by fear for the dog, and by how much she has come to matter
quotes: "My hands were shaking on the wheel, which surprised me. I am usually all right in an emergency, I am the one people ring. … And underneath all of it there was this other thing going on, which was, when did I let something matter this much."
notes: Her competence gone, her voice a stranger's. The dog's silence read as knowing. Underneath, the question of when this happened.

Initial:49:0.text: Tears of relief held back until the car park
quotes: "And I sat in the car afterwards and cried, which I had not done in the waiting room, I saved that up for the car park. Relief, obviously."
notes: Bathos, told against herself. The tears kept for the car. Not embarrassment, shock, she corrects.

Initial:51:0.text: Grief for the dog found ready in advance, and not welcome
quotes: "She had a thorn in her foot and I had spent twenty minutes organising my own grief in advance, in traffic. … So that Saturday was a rehearsal. And I did not enjoy finding out that I have got the whole thing ready to go."
notes: Grief already prepared. She is six, and lurchers are not a forty year proposition. The rehearsal tells her it is coming.

Initial:53:0.text: Trying not to think of the dog's death, and laughing herself out of it
quotes: "I try not to. I am aware that is not much of an answer. It sits there. … it is a waste of a Tuesday evening to sit there grieving a dog who is snoring at you."
notes: Not much of an answer, she says. The running legs, and the thought she stops. She laughs herself out of it.

Initial:57:0.text: Lost in a wrong quiet without the dog
quotes: "The first time I thought, brilliant, two hours, I will get so much done. And I came back into the house and stood in the kitchen and did not know what to do with myself. It was so quiet. And it was not a nice quiet, it was a wrong quiet"
notes: The free time does not arrive. The quiet is wrong, a noise only noticed once it stops. The stair again, empty now.

Initial:59:0.text: The house 'on standby' without the dog
quotes: "Er. It was like the house was on standby. Everything in it is arranged around her now, and we never sat down and decided to arrange it. … And with her not in it the whole place was just a set. Furniture waiting for somebody."
notes: Standby, then a set: the house not lived in without her. Nothing was decided, it was arranged. The rule on the chair is going the way of the others.

Initial:63:0.text: A bit alarming, how much of home rests on the dog
quotes: "I suppose because of how much is resting on her. If a house can go flat for two hours, what happens when it is not two hours. That is the thought I do not let myself finish."
notes: Two hours flat, and then what of longer. All of it on someone who cannot know she carries it.

Initial:65:0.text: Real fun in doing the dog's voices together
quotes: "It is genuinely the funniest thing in that house. And I do think that is real, that is not us avoiding anything, that is just a good thing we have got hold of."
notes: Laughter she defends as real, and then times. Half nine: when the voices come out.

Initial:67:0.text: Escaping hard talk through the dog
quotes: "There is a list. … But the dog is a very good door to close on it. She comes and puts her chin on your knee at about that time, and it is completely legitimate to stop talking and make a fuss of her instead."
notes: The list given in full, for once: money, next year, her mother. The chin on the knee as the legitimate way out.

Initial:69:0.text: Relieved by the dog's interruption, then a bit uneasy at the relief
quotes: "Relieved, because I do not want to do the list at half nine either. And then a bit uneasy, because being relieved is a sign of something, isn't it."
"But then I think, she is also the reason we are in the same room at all. Before her we would be on separate floors doing separate things and calling it an evening."
notes: She names her own pattern, two ways at once. Separate floors before her, and now the sofa with a dog laid between them.

Initial:69:1.text: The dog the reason the couple share a room at all
quotes: "Relieved, because I do not want to do the list at half nine either. And then a bit uneasy, because being relieved is a sign of something, isn't it."
"But then I think, she is also the reason we are in the same room at all. Before her we would be on separate floors doing separate things and calling it an evening."
notes: She names her own pattern, two ways at once. Separate floors before her, and now the sofa with a dog laid between them.

Initial:73:0.text: Goodnight to the dog out loud: a ridiculous ritual she could not skip
quotes: "And the last thing that happens every night is that I go in and say goodnight to her, out loud, like she is a person … It is the most ridiculous ritual and if I ever skipped it I think I would lie there upstairs thinking about it."
notes: The rule held, more or less. The blanket was hers once. Two thumps counted exactly, and a ritual she could not skip.

Initial:75:0.text: More patience for the dog than for the people at home, and she knows it
quotes: "And maybe the other one, which is that I know I am kinder to her than I am to the people in my house. … I do not know what to do about that, but I do know it."
notes: Two things unsaid, the first year and her unevenness. She knows it and does not know what to do about it.

Initial:79:0.text: The dog become part of home through ordinary days
quotes: "None of this is dramatic. … And somewhere in all that ordinary stuff she has got herself right into the middle of the house, and I could not tell you which day that happened. There was no day. It is just that now, if you asked me to describe home, she would be in the description"
notes: Her own summary, ordinary and wet. There was no day it happened. Home is described with the dog in it, without a thought first.

pets.title: “Shut in” after Dennis died, until the dog opened the door
pets.description: A still house come alive with someone in it to tell, and a reason to get up, eat and be among people again

pets.title: “Like having the lights on”: the house alive again
pets.description: Mess, a listener and breathing in the night, where things used to stay put

pets.title: Needed again, and out among people without trying
pets.description: Up at seven, eating properly, and a morning society on the green

pets.title: Holding on to Pepper, and to her own say over her life
pets.description: After the fall and her daughter's “the dog has to go”, frightened and sure by morning, and patient until the dog and her daughter came round

pets.title: Lighter for knowing Pepper will not be left waiting when she dies
pets.description: A dog likely to outlive her, provided for in her will, so the picture of her waiting at the window can be put down

Initial:3:0.text: A dog like having the lights on
quotes: "It's like having the lights on. That's the nearest I can get to it."
notes: Her image is light, not noise, though the noise comes first as a joke. Before, a cup still there in the morning.

Initial:5:0.text: Glad of the mess: after two still years, signs of life in the house
quotes: "So it's a funny thing to be glad of. But a house where things stay put is a house where nothing's happening. I had two years of that and I don't want it back. … It means somebody's been living here."
notes: Two years of stillness, named plainly. The glasses case in the dog's bed counts as evidence of life.

Initial:7:0.text: Up at seven for the dog, where before there was nothing to get up for
quotes: "Before her I'd lie there till nine some days, there wasn't anything to get up for. … Now it's seven o'clock, dressing gown, kettle on, let her out, and we're on the green by half past. Rain or shine."
notes: The days before had no start. A polite insistence, felt through the eyelids. New clothes for a new routine.

Initial:9:0.text: Through the dog, a morning society she never knew was there
quotes: "Oh, it's a whole society. You wouldn't know it unless you had a dog. … I'd lived on this estate twenty years and I didn't know them."
notes: A world there all along, opened to her with the dog. She knows its etiquette and explains it.

Initial:11:0.text: Back among people without having to try, after losing the habit
quotes: "It's lovely. I don't want to overdo it, but it's saved me a bit. … I'd lost the habit. You forget how. And with a dog you don't need to know how … the talking just happens round the edges."
notes: No effort asked of her, the dog is the reason to be there. Help given as well as taken.

Initial:13:0.text: With the dog depending on her, eating properly again after a bad winter
quotes: "But I was in a bad way that second winter on my own. … And now I've got to be up and out and someone's depending on me, and you can't feed a dog and not feed yourself, it looks ridiculous. So I eat. I sit down to it."
notes: She plays down her own word, saved. Feeding the dog and feeding herself go together in her telling.

Initial:15:0.text: Six months of thinking the dog a terrible mistake
quotes: "No. Oh, no. The first six months I thought I'd made a terrible mistake."
notes: Doubt at the start, told with humour. The fall comes quickly, almost comic.

Initial:17:0.text: Her daughter's care felt as being treated like a child
quotes: "She thought she was looking after me, and she was, I know she was. But it felt like she was taking something off me. Like I was a child who'd been given a puppy and couldn't be trusted with it."
notes: She grants her daughter's care and still feels something taken from her.

Initial:19:0.text: Feeling small, and frightened for herself and the dog
quotes: "I felt small. And frightened too, if I'm honest, because she had a point, hadn't she. … what if it had been my hip. What happens to her then. What happens to me."
"I didn't sleep much. But I knew I wasn't giving her up. I knew that by the morning."
notes: The night in the sling, two fears side by side. The decision is there by morning, without argument.

Initial:19:1.text: Sure by morning she was keeping the dog
quotes: "I felt small. And frightened too, if I'm honest, because she had a point, hadn't she. … what if it had been my hip. What happens to her then. What happens to me."
"I didn't sleep much. But I knew I wasn't giving her up. I knew that by the morning."
notes: The night in the sling, two fears side by side. The decision is there by morning, without argument.

Initial:21:0.text: Learning patience with the dog at seventy three, and it paying off, mostly
quotes: "I took her to classes. At my age! … It takes forever. The first week it took us forty minutes to get to the end of the road. But she learned. She walks nicely now, mostly."
notes: At my age: pride as much as surprise. Patience as her answer to the fall.

Initial:23:0.text: Peace with her daughter, unspoken, shown in a chew
quotes: "We've not talked about it since, really. But she brings Pepper a chew when she comes now. That's how I know."
notes: Mending without talking about it. She finds it in the chew.

Initial:25:0.text: Providing for a dog likely to outlive her, practical more than gloomy
quotes: "Not in a gloomy way. Well, sometimes in a gloomy way. But mostly practical. … She could well outlive me. So I've sorted it. … My daughter thought that was morbid. I think it's the most responsible thing I've ever done."
notes: The losing turned round: her own death and the dog's future. Responsible, she says, not morbid.

Initial:29:0.text: Lighter once the dog's future was settled
quotes: "But I came out and sat on the wall outside and I felt lighter. Like I'd put something down. Because it had been sitting with me, the not knowing, every time she looked at me."
notes: The will sets the dog among Dennis's things and the house. Relief in the body, on the wall outside.

Initial:31:0.text: Unable to bear the thought of the dog waiting and her never coming
quotes: "When I go to the shops she's at the window when I come back. Every time. … And I couldn't bear the thought of her doing that and me never coming."
notes: Waiting is the image that carries it. Her own death matters here as the dog's loss.

Initial:33:0.text: Telling the dog her day, as she once told Dennis
quotes: "And sometimes I catch myself and think, Mabel, you're telling a dog the price of butter. But it's a habit of forty years, telling someone about your day. It had nowhere to go. Now it goes to her."
notes: The habit of a marriage finds a listener. She laughs at herself and keeps on.

Initial:35:0.text: Glad of the dog's breathing in the night, on his side of the bed
quotes: "She's on the bed now. On his side. … But it's nice to hear breathing. I'll say that and leave it there. It's nice to hear breathing in the night again."
notes: She closes the subject herself, I'll say that and leave it there. The side of the bed is his.

Initial:37:0.text: Opened out of a shut-in life by the dog, and mostly glad
quotes: "Only that I didn't expect it. Any of it. … She opened the door, really, that's what it is. I was shut in and she opened the door. Some mornings I'd still rather she hadn't, when it's sleeting. But mostly I'm glad."
notes: Her own summary, sleet and all. Glad, said twice.

pets.title: Giving her up, and not knowing “whether I failed her”
pets.description: A relief he is ashamed of, the fault taken as his, and three months of telling himself she is better off

pets.title: Letting her go, with a relief he is ashamed of
pets.description: Awful and a relief, a week of feeling he was lying to her, and her not looking back

pets.title: The fault taken as his, never the dog's
pets.description: A flat she could not live in, everything tried, and knowing before he was told

pets.title: Glad for her, and still unsettled three months on
pets.description: Better off, he says every day, and he cannot know if he failed her

pets.title: Still holding on to a dog he let go
pets.description: Her absence lived in his body and his flat, and her bowl, her sock and her good name kept

pets.title: Her absence lived in his body and his flat
pets.description: Arms with nothing to hold, still on guard in the street, still awake at quarter past five

pets.title: Her bowl, her sock and her good name, kept
pets.description: Frightened, never a problem, and remembered in the odd socks

pets.title: The best company he has had, in a life “arranged round her”
pets.description: Company and peace in a lonely time, and a life closed in round her fear before he saw it

pets.title: Company and peace in a lonely time
pets.description: A dog at his knee under the desk, and frosty mornings that were theirs

pets.title: A life closed in round her fear, unnoticed
pets.description: Walks in the dark at both ends, always listening, never able to leave her, and nobody asking any more

Initial:3:0.text: The dog gone but still in the present tense
quotes: "She went in the summer, so I keep starting to say it is and then it's was."
notes: Tense trouble from the first lines: gone, and still in the present tense. Everything, meant both ways, as warmth and as weight.

Initial:5:0.text: The dog his best company in a lonely time
quotes: "She was the best company I've ever had, honestly, and she came at a point where I didn't have much company. … And then there's this dog leaning on my knee under the desk."
"But the other way is that she took over. Everything had to be arranged round her. Every single thing. And I didn't see it happening until it had already happened."
notes: Whole days without speaking, then a dog at his knee. The taking over is only visible once it has happened.

Initial:5:1.text: Taken over by the dog's needs before he saw it
quotes: "She was the best company I've ever had, honestly, and she came at a point where I didn't have much company. … And then there's this dog leaning on my knee under the desk."
"But the other way is that she took over. Everything had to be arranged round her. Every single thing. And I didn't see it happening until it had already happened."
notes: Whole days without speaking, then a dog at his knee. The taking over is only visible once it has happened.

Initial:7:0.text: Days pushed into the dark round the dog's fear, not really a joke
quotes: "If she saw one, even right across the park, she'd go up on her back legs and scream at it. Not bark. Scream. … Half five in the morning and then again at eleven at night. Dark at both ends. I used to joke I'd gone nocturnal. I wasn't really joking."
notes: A timetable built round her fear of other dogs. Scream, not bark: he corrects his own word to give its size.

Initial:9:0.text: Some walks in the frost lovely, and theirs alone
quotes: "Some of them were lovely, actually. … And I'd stand in the middle with my coffee and think, this is all right, this is ours."
"But I was always listening. Even when she was happy I was listening for a car door, or a jingle, someone else's dog. I never stopped listening, the whole time I had her."
notes: Joy and watchfulness in one moment. The lovely walks sit inside the listening, never apart from it.

Initial:9:1.text: Always listening for another dog, even in the lovely moments
quotes: "Some of them were lovely, actually. … And I'd stand in the middle with my coffee and think, this is all right, this is ours."
"But I was always listening. Even when she was happy I was listening for a car door, or a jingle, someone else's dog. I never stopped listening, the whole time I had her."
notes: Joy and watchfulness in one moment. The lovely walks sit inside the listening, never apart from it.

Initial:11:0.text: Strange to find his body still on guard for a dog no longer there
quotes: "That's the strange bit. … I was halfway across before I thought, what are you doing, you haven't got a dog. My body was still doing it for her."
notes: The watchfulness outlasts her. He finds it out halfway across the road, in his body before his thinking.

Initial:13:0.text: The dog's closeness lovely, and confining
quotes: "Which is lovely, and it was lovely, but it also meant I couldn't really go anywhere. She couldn't be left."
notes: Tenderness and confinement in one image, the head on the foot. Home narrows to the flat and the car.

Initial:15:0.text: Life narrowed round the dog, not felt as a loss at the time
quotes: "I'd stopped saying yes to things so long ago that people had stopped asking. So it's hard to say what it was like, because I didn't feel it as a loss while it was going on. … The dog was the reason, and it's a good reason, nobody argues with it."
notes: Someone else names it first. The dog as a good reason, and so nobody asks.

Initial:17:0.text: Unable to keep the dog, or anyone, safe in that flat
quotes: "And I stood in the hall reading it with Skye leaning on my legs and I thought, I can't keep her safe here. Or I can't keep everyone else safe. One of those."
notes: The letter in his hand, her weight against his legs. Safety splits two ways and he leaves it split.

Initial:19:0.text: Taking the blame for a life the dog could not live
quotes: "I've gone back and forth on which. … That I'd put her in a life she couldn't do. … That wasn't her fault. That was mine."
notes: The blame moves over time, from everyone else to her life to himself. She stays blameless throughout.

Initial:21:0.text: Trying everything, and already knowing the dog needed a different life
quotes: "I tried everything first. … Nothing was going to help on the stairs. … And I knew what she meant before she'd finished saying it."
notes: On the record: he wants it known that he tried. The behaviourist's sentence lands before it ends.

Initial:23:0.text: Awful and a relief, and still a bit ashamed of the relief
quotes: "Awful. And a relief. Both at once, and I was ashamed of the relief, I still am a bit."
"And she'd be doing her loops round the tennis courts and I felt like I was lying to her. Which is mad, she's a dog. But that's what it felt like."
notes: A week of saying nothing. A secret kept from a dog who cannot know it, and still felt as a lie.

Initial:23:1.text: Feeling he was lying to the dog, mad as he knows it is
quotes: "Awful. And a relief. Both at once, and I was ashamed of the relief, I still am a bit."
"And she'd be doing her loops round the tennis courts and I felt like I was lying to her. Which is mad, she's a dog. But that's what it felt like."
notes: A week of saying nothing. A secret kept from a dog who cannot know it, and still felt as a lie.

Initial:25:0.text: Comforted by the dog as if she knew
quotes: "And Skye came and put her head in my lap. Like she knew. She didn't know, she just saw me on the floor and came over. But it felt like she knew."
notes: The yes comes before the details. He corrects himself, she did not know, and lets the feeling stand.

Initial:27:0.text: Watching the dog go without looking back, as he'd want
quotes: "and she looked back at me once. Then she went off with the man to see the field. She didn't look back again. Which is what you'd want. I know that's what you'd want."
notes: He wants to take her himself. Not looking back is what you would want, he says, twice over.

Initial:31:0.text: Emptied by her going, in his arms and in the flat
quotes: "I just felt very light, like my arms didn't have anything to hold. And then I drove home, and the flat was, it was just a flat."
"I've still got her bowl, actually. It's in the cupboard under the sink. I don't know why I've kept it."
notes: Light as in empty, the body again. The bowl is kept under the sink, out of sight and never thrown away.

Initial:33:0.text: Still waking at her hour with nothing to get up for
quotes: "Quiet. Very quiet. I still wake up at quarter past five, three months on. Every day. I lie there and there's nothing to get up for, so I just lie there."
"And I look at that and think, good. Good, she's happy. And then I put the phone face down on the table for a bit."
notes: The old timetable goes on without her. Good news on the screen, and the screen turned over.

Initial:33:1.text: Glad of her photos, and needing to put them face down for a bit

notes: The old timetable goes on without her. Good news on the screen, and the screen turned over.

Initial:35:0.text: Needing to say every day she is better off: not settled
quotes: "It's like I'm glad and something else at the same time, and the something else hasn't got a name yet. … But I notice I have to keep saying it. If it was settled I wouldn't need to say it every day, would I."
notes: He takes his own repetition as a sign. Unsettled, and he knows it.

Initial:37:0.text: Not knowing if he failed her, and no one to tell him
quotes: "I think I'd want to know first whether I failed her or whether I did the right thing for her, and I don't know that, and I'm not sure anyone can tell me."
notes: Open, and named as open. A question he does not expect anyone to answer for him.

Initial:39:0.text: The dog never a problem, only frightened
quotes: "She wasn't a problem. She was frightened. There's a difference. With me, in the flat, with the door shut, she was the gentlest thing."
"Every morning for eighteen months I got one sock. I still find odd socks in the washing and think of her. Stupid, really."
notes: He defends her against his own telling. He ends on the sock, small and daily.

groups.label: A home come alive with the dog, and gone flat without her
groups.description: Lights on again for Mabel, a house never empty for Juno until two hours at the groomer's, and for Rowan arms with nothing to hold and a flat that is just a flat

groups.label: The dog a way back to people, or a way round them
groups.description: Mabel back among people on the green, Rowan cut off behind a reason nobody argues with, and Juno finding the dog easier than the people at home

groups.label: Changed by the dog in ways none of them saw coming
groups.description: Juno caught going soft, Mabel opened out of a shut-in life and Rowan taken over, each changed before they saw it happen, and each in a different direction

groups.label: Holding on to the dog through what it costs, or letting her go
groups.description: Mabel keeps Pepper through a fall and her daughter's fears, Juno through a regret never said and a night that cost her, and Rowan gives Skye up and takes the fault as his

groups.label: The parting from the dog, faced ahead of time or still unsettled after
groups.description: Juno finds her grief rehearsed on a false alarm, Mabel provides for a dog likely to outlive her, and Rowan, three months on, still keeps Skye in his body and his cupboard
